title: Rebalance host IO scheduling and coalesce GPU copies to reduce threadpool contention
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Our host-side pipeline still accounts for 20-35% of end-to-end latency p95 for common short-sequence workloads. Root causes observed in traces: (1) many small CPU->GPU memcpy ops (scatter of ~<8KB transfers) that do not saturate PCIe/AVA, (2) excessive wakeups on the host threadpool from per-request scheduling decisions, and (3) suboptimal ordering of prefill vs decode kernel launches when multiple concurrent clients share a GPU, leading to reduced kernel occupancy. This ticket targets a host-level strategy to reduce overhead by coalescing small copies, rebalancing IO scheduling to minimize context switches, and coordinating kernel selection heuristics with the host scheduler to improve occupancy and tail latency.
technical_details: Planned changes: (a) introduce a copy coalescer in the host DMA layer that aggregates temporally adjacent small host->device transfers per-GPU per-interval (configurable window 200-800us) and issues a single batched memcpy when beneficial; (b) add a lightweight host IO scheduler that groups prefill and short decode tasks to reduce threadpool wakeups and enforce a bounded concurrency cap for small-reqs to avoid thread thrash; (c) extend kernel-selection policy to expose expected active-slot counts so the scheduler can prefer kernels with better packing characteristics for concurrent small inferences; (d) fast-path zero-copy fallback for >8KB contiguous tensors to preserve current zero-copy benefits. Implementation will live in host/driver/{dma, scheduler} and runtime/selector modules.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end p95 latency on short-seq (<=64 tokens) workloads reduced by >=15% in our internal benchmark compared to baseline; 2) Host CPU utilization for inference-serving processes reduced by >=20% under 500 concurrent short-req clients; 3) No regression (>1% token error) in output correctness for existing eval prompt sets; 4) Feature gated and control-plane config exposed via runtime-1.22 for canary rollout.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for coalescer state machine and windowing heuristics.
- Microbench: synthetic 1-8KB memcpy bursts with mocked NIC to confirm coalesce reduction and latency impact.
- Integration perf: run open-internal short-seq harness across dedicated and shared GPU profiles and compare baseline vs feature-on.
- Chaos: simulate slow PCIe transfers and preemption to ensure scheduler fallback does not deadlock.
- Telemetry: add metrics: coalesced_bytes, coalesced_ops, scheduler_wakeups, small_req_concurrency, kernel_pack_score.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind gflag runtime.host_copy_coalesce and runtime.host_sched_bounded_small_reqs; 2) Canary on staging with 5% traffic for two days; 3) Expand to 25% on dedicated pools, observe metrics for 48h; 4) Gradual ramp to 100% across hosted, with ability to revert via config. Include a kill-switch for immediate disable.
rollback_criteria:
- p95 latency increases >5% for core customer workloads for >30 minutes after rollout step.
- Error rate increase >0.5% absolute in any region.
- CPU utilization increases >10% compared to baseline for two consecutive hours.
open_risks:
- Coalescing window tuning may harm latency for single large interactive requests if misconfigured.
- Scheduler bounding could reduce throughput for large-batch inference jobs if per-tenant policies not respected.
- Kernel selection hints require coordination with selector team to avoid double-counting occupancy estimates.
tasks: design coalescer API and window heuristic
implement host IO scheduler and bounded small-req queue
